title: C.A.R.E Collaborative
description: The C.A.R.E. Collaborative is a multi-site QI project implemented across seven long-term care homes in British Columbia and focused on reducing unnecessary and avoidable emergency department transfers from long-term care facilities.

title: Waste Segregation in the Operating Room
photoAlt: Waste Segregation in the Operating Room
description: This project aimed to improve waste segregation in the anesthesiology OR at St. Boniface Hospital and reduce unnecessary incineration of medical waste. Previously, a single pharmaceutical waste bin was used for mixed OR waste, which was then transported to Minnesota for high-carbon incineration. However, evidence suggests that most OR waste can instead be autoclaved or landfilled with lower environmental impact and cost. A new segregation system was therefore introduced with separate bins for sharps, pharmaceutical liquids, and general waste, supported by education sessions and ongoing staff coaching.

title: SE-QI Toolkit as an Engagement tool
photoAlt: SE-QI Toolkit as an Engagement tool
description: The initiative involved using the SE-QI Toolkit to support sustainability-focused quality improvement work within Northern Health, particularly in relation to clinical ideas such as reducing single-use materials, such as disposable patient gowns, and improving resource stewardship.
toolkitApplication: The Toolkit was used during meetings with clinical teams by inputting project ideas and guiding users through Steps 1–3 to explore sustainability opportunities and interpret outputs. It also helped identify relevant resources and demonstrated the Toolkit’s accessibility and practical utility for users unfamiliar with the field of planetary health.
toolkitAudienceUptake: The primary audience has been clinical teams and individuals initiating sustainability-related QI projects. Uptake has been early-stage and exploratory, with the Toolkit mainly used as an engagement and education tool.
mostValuableElements: Step 2 of the Toolkit was identified as the most valuable component due to its clear, structured presentation of resources that helped avoid unnecessary complexity. It enabled users to efficiently identify relevant pathways and supported quicker decision-making without requiring extensive independent research.
qiIntegrationComments: There is strong potential for the Toolkit to be integrated into routine QI work within Northern Health. Given limited capacity in current care models and few dedicated sustainability roles, the Toolkit could help provide structure and direction for teams pioneering people-oriented clinical sustainability initiatives.

title: Decrease of Personal Protective Device Failures
photoAlt: Decrease of Personal Protective Device Failures
description: An initiative at St. Paul’s Hospital aimed to reduce failures of personal protective devices caused by depleted batteries in the Psychiatric Assessment and Stabilization Unit. A structured inventory control and battery replacement process was introduced to improve equipment reliability, enhance staff and patient safety, and reduce disruptions to care.
cobenefit:
The Toolkit supports broader systems thinking by highlighting downstream effects, trade-offs, and co-benefits even in projects with mixed environmental implications.

title: Integrating the SE-QI Toolkit in ONSQIN
photoAlt: Integrating the SE-QI Toolkit in ONSQIN
description: An early-stage initiative involving exploration of the SE-QI Toolkit as a potential future resource to be introduced and disseminated to clinicians through Ontario Health’s Closing the Quality Gap campaign. title: Prompting Re-Assessment of Antidepressant Prescriptions

title: Reducing the Climate Impact of Metered-Dose Inhalers
photoAlt: Reducing the Climate Impact of Metered-Dose Inhalers
description: This project was a collaboration between a primary care pharmacist and a family physician to reduce the environmental impact of inhaler prescribing in primary care. The initiative focused on optimizing respiratory care by assessing whether inhalers were needed, identifying opportunities for deprescribing when clinically appropriate, switching patients to lower-carbon dry powder inhalers, and providing education on inhaler disposal. Patients’ experiences with team-based care were also explored, including the role of sustainability considerations and the value of in-depth conversations in healthcare decision-making.
cobenefit: The Toolkit offers helpful reinforcement of existing knowledge and the reminder to consistently apply a sustainability lens when completing quality improvement work.

title: Health Quality BC’s Quality Academy
description: Health Quality BC’s Quality Academy is a six-month professional development program that builds learners’ capability to lead quality and safety initiatives through formal instruction, mentorship, and an applied improvement project. The SE-QI Toolkit is now embedded in a dedicated session that explores how sustainability can be incorporated into quality improvement.
toolkitApplication: Learners are introduced to the SE-QI Toolkit and encouraged to apply it to their Quality Academy projects. They use the Toolkit to identify practical opportunities to incorporate sustainability considerations and relevant measures into the planning, implementation, and evaluation of their improvement work. This supports the program’s existing competencies related to measurement, systems thinking, and incorporating sustainability into quality improvement initiatives.
toolkitAudienceUptake:
The initiative is intended for Quality Academy learners from across British Columbia’s
health system, including clinical and non-clinical professionals from acute, primary,
community, long-term, residential, mental health, and other care settings who are
leading improvement projects.
In 2026, 16 Quality Academy participants identified how their QA projects aligned with
environmental sustainability in the Aligning Quality and Environmental Sustainability
session.
mostValuableElements: The most valuable components are the structured prompts that help teams identify sustainability opportunities, consider potential impacts across their projects, and select meaningful sustainability measures. The Toolkit’s practical and step-by-step format makes it adaptable to a wide range of Quality Academy projects and care settings.
qiIntegrationComments: The SE-QI Toolkit is now embedded within Health Quality BC’s Quality Academy as part of a dedicated session on integrating sustainability into quality improvement.

title: Healthcare Excellence Canada’s EXTRA Program
description: Healthcare Excellence Canada’s EXTRA program is a team-based, action-oriented leadership development program that supports healthcare leaders to advance quality, safety, and system transformation through applied improvement projects. The SE-QI Toolkit is now included within the EXTRA curriculum to strengthen participants’ capacity to integrate sustainability into their improvement work.
toolkitApplication: Two learning sessions are dedicated to sustainability during an in-person residency. The first introduces sustainable health systems and their connection to healthcare quality and improvement. The second introduces the SE-QI Toolkit and provides teams with dedicated time to apply it to their EXTRA improvement projects, identify relevant sustainability opportunities and impacts, and explore potential actions and measures.
toolkitAudienceUptake:
The target audience is EXTRA fellows participating in interdisciplinary teams from healthcare and social service organizations across Canada. Participants include healthcare leaders, people with lived experience, policy advisors and analysts, and quality and safety improvement leaders working on organizational or system-level improvement projects.
As the Toolkit’s inclusion in the curriculum is new, uptake will be assessed through participants’ engagement during the residency and its subsequent application within their EXTRA improvement projects.
mostValuableElements: The practical, step-by-step format helps teams translate broad sustainability concepts into concrete actions and relevant measures that can be incorporated into their existing improvement plans.
qiIntegrationComments:
The SE-QI Toolkit is now embedded within Healthcare Excellence Canada’s EXTRA curriculum through dedicated learning on sustainable health systems and the application of the Toolkit to participants’ improvement projects.
There is also potential to further integrate the Toolkit into other formal leadership-development, quality-improvement, coaching, and capacity-building programs offered by Healthcare Excellence Canada.

title: Home Pan-Canadian Network Pan-Canadian Network on Health System Response to Climate Change
photoAlt: Home Pan-Canadian Network Pan-Canadian Network on Health System Response to Climate Change
description:
The CASCADES Pan-Canadian Practice Network connects healthcare professionals and organizations across Canada to build capacity, exchange knowledge, and advance environmentally sustainable health systems. Within the Network, the SE-QI Working Group, co-chaired by Vancouver Coastal Health and Healthcare Excellence Canada, brings together representatives from participating organizations to advance the integration of sustainability into quality improvement practice.
The Working Group supports the mobilization, application, and continued improvement of the SE-QI Framework, Toolkit, and Spotlight, while fostering shared learning across organizations and helping strengthen the field of sustainability-embedded quality improvement in Canada.
toolkitApplication:
Participating organizations apply the SE-QI Toolkit to quality improvement projects, capacity-building initiatives, and/or educational programs within their respective settings. Working Group meetings provide opportunities for members to share how the Toolkit is being used, discuss implementation experiences and challenges, and identify opportunities to strengthen its content and usability.
Members are also supported to embed the Toolkit within existing organizational structures and programs and to develop submissions for the SE-QI Spotlight. These examples help mobilize learning within the Network and more broadly across the Canadian health system.
toolkitAudienceUptake:
The initiative is intended for healthcare professionals, quality improvement leaders, sustainability and planetary health leaders, educators, and organizational partners from organizations participating in the Pan-Canadian Practice Network who are seeking to integrate sustainability into improvement initiatives. 
As of July 2026, the SE-QI Working Group includes 19 participants representing 12 local or regional healthcare organizations, one pan-Canadian organization, and four provinces. Participating organizations are at different stages of implementation: some have applied the Toolkit to specific improvement projects, while others are exploring opportunities to embed it within formal QI programs, educational initiatives, and organizational processes.
mostValuableElements: The identification of key SE-QI principles and the Toolkit’s structured, guided approach are particularly valuable, as they help teams make clear connections between quality improvement and sustainability. The inclusion of practical calculators within the Toolkit’s resources is also valuable, as it makes it easier for teams to quantify relevant environmental and other sustainability impacts.
qiIntegrationComments: The SE-QI Toolkit is already embedded at the centre of the Working Group’s activities, providing participating organizations with a shared foundation, common language, and practical tools to integrate sustainability into quality improvement.
